name: Rotating polytrope
blurb: The polytrope (n = 1 by default) spinning rigidly at Ω = 0.4 about z, at rest in a frame that turns with it (the rotating frame, on the gravity page): settled into balance with the centrifugal force as well as gravity, it starts flattened at the poles and holds that shape. One dynamical time is t = 1; one turn is t = 2π / Ω. Its equator's thin outer layers need about 128 cells across the box to stay still.
